claim: Latent learning: rats given no reward for several days then rewarded drop errors sharply, which Tolman reads as an unexpressed map. Reported with figures only, no statistics; a motivation account is not excluded.
agent_test: Design principle only: exploration without reward should still be stored in the map.

claim: A broad map (states plus moves) survives a changed start or blocked route; a stored single route does not (Tolman strip vs comprehensive map; model SR-TD fails detours).
agent_test: Block a move or move the goal mid-task; compare an agent with an explicit state-move list vs a stored plan at equal tokens.

claim: In humans, reward revaluation is easier than transition (detour) revaluation, as a successor representation predicts; policy revaluation is also hard. Study I N=58 (0.520 vs 0.450, t(57)=2.89); Study II N=88 (switch 0.659 vs 0.466, Z=-2.85).
agent_test: Run reward, transition and policy change tasks on the agent; expect the same ordering; test whether a re-plan operator after a transition change closes the gap.

claim: Cached predictive structure alone (SR-TD) fails detours and policy change; adding replay (Dyna) fixes it. A map needs a revision-by-simulation step, not only a stored table. Gap search: in GAVEL graph-derived repair beat asking the LLM to replan (67.7 vs 55.4 on 4B, 1 vs 3.4 LLM calls).
agent_test: Ablate the re-plan step after a blocked move; measure success at equal tokens.

claim: A hexagonal (6-fold) grid-like signal in entorhinal cortex and vmPFC appears for abstract 2-D conceptual space (N=28, entorhinal Z=4.41; no effect at 4,5,7,8-fold).
agent_test: Not agent-testable; brain evidence only.

claim: Replications of the conceptual grid-like code are mixed: young adults 6-fold t(19)=3.71, older adults none; a 2024 study (N=38) found the entorhinal ROI 'less consistent'; a 2019 preprint reports a null in vmPFC (not opened). The grid claim is fragile. Gap search 2026-11-03: Park 2021 (N=21, 6-fold in EC and mPFC, stable across days) and Theves 2020 (N=25, EC only, mPFC null, pre/post contrast p=0.07) are positive but small and selected; Kransberg 2026 (N=110, passive spatial navigation) found no 6-fold signal (BF01 7.3 right EC). No abstract-space replication above N=30 was found.
agent_test: None. Do not build the schema on grid-cell details.

claim: Humans organise abstract relational knowledge so response time follows graph communicability (multi-path), not link distance or Euclidean distance (RT t(25)=2.77; fMRI N=23).
agent_test: Ask the agent to judge relatedness on a graph; compare multi-path vs shortest-path distance as predictors.

claim: Hippocampal-entorhinal neurons code a non-spatial continuous variable (sound frequency) in rats: 40.0 percent of CA1 and 51.3 percent of MEC cells task-modulated.
agent_test: None directly; supports a general map format.

claim: Reward locations restructure the grid code: median grid rotation 12.53 deg, 49 of 102 grid cells changed (7 rats). Goal skew of maps is real in rodents.
agent_test: Mark the goal and its predecessors in the written state map; test search success at equal tokens.

claim: Humans build a Euclidean 2-D map from pairwise relations and infer unseen relations at 93.6 percent (N=27 analysed of 33; only 82 of 282 passed training).
agent_test: Give the agent pairwise relations only; test whether writing an explicit coordinate layout beats a list of pairs.

claim: TEM-style models explain place/grid remapping and relational inference (family tree) with one structure-learning mechanism; transformer version TEM-t is far more sample-efficient. Computational support only.
agent_test: Supports a reusable abstract structure kept separate from entity identity; test by renaming entities in the task.

claim: LLM planning on cognitive-map tasks: GPT-4 near ceiling at 1-step paths (0.99) but 2-step 0.82, 3-step 0.55, n-step 0.47; policy revaluation worst (0.21). Small models 0.04-0.06 at 3 steps. Re-checked in arXiv text of CogEval.
agent_test: Replicate CogEval graphs with scaffold vs plain prompt at equal tokens.

claim: GPT-4 fails shortest path across graph clusters: 0 of 30 at temperature 0, never above 10 percent at other temperatures; edge hallucination reported.
agent_test: Count invalid edges in the agent's written map; add an edge check against the task text.

claim: Graph-search hints (BFS/DFS) help only some tasks and temperatures; chain of thought helps non-teleporting shortcuts (1.00) but not teleporting ones (0.50).
agent_test: Compare hint-in-prompt vs an operator that runs explicit BFS in the scratchpad.

claim: Writing a cognitive map before planning helps only after training: fine-tuned optimal-plan rate 76.5 percent vs 19.0 (no CoT) and 26.5 (best CoT); prompting a map alone gave 0-1 percent in most models; plain DFS (94.5 reachable) beat the map (88.5). Re-checked in arXiv text. Gap search: few-shot (0-4 demos) map prompting gave 0-10 percent for o1, GPT-4o and Llama-3, while o1 with no map prompt reached 38 percent at 4-shot; trained DFS 94.5 vs trained map 88.5.
agent_test: Prompt-only map-then-plan vs plain CoT at equal tokens on a maze task. Prior: no gain for strong models.

claim: Visualising state after each step (VoT) raised GPT-4 language navigation from 35.50 to 59.00 (+23.5) but was not significant vs CoT (about 54.00, p<0.16); state-visualisation accuracy only 24-26 percent. Re-checked.
agent_test: Add a redraw-state step after each move; compare redrawn state with ground truth.

claim: An external topological map improved a 3B model from 64.40 to 81.20 percent (about 2.52 refinement rounds), beating CoT self-consistency k=5 (59.80). One preprint, small models, 500 problems. Re-checked.
agent_test: Replicate on a strong model; check whether gain vanishes as in MAP.

claim: Map-then-act (MAP) on a 4B model: ReAct to MAP 31.8 to 61.1 (ALFWorld), 31.8 to 71.9 (TextCraft), 13.9 to 24.3 (SciWorld); strong models near 99 gain little. Re-checked in PDF table. Gap search: the grounded-model gain also falls with backbone strength in Hybrid-WM (+26 for Llama-3-8B to +4 for GPT-4o-mini); but a checked graph model still lifts Claude Sonnet 5 from 38.6 to 99.4 (GAVEL).
agent_test: Build the map first then act, on a weak model; measure vs ReAct at equal tokens. Expect little gain on strong models.

claim: LLMs encode space and time linearly in activations (Llama-2-70b R2: world 0.911, NYC 0.359); generalisation to held-out blocks is worse (proximity error 0.164 vs 0.071).
agent_test: Probe evidence: maps exist inside models; says nothing about scaffold benefit.

claim: Maze-trained transformers form probeable maze representations; best model 70.7 percent exact on out-of-distribution mazes, hallway model 24.2.
agent_test: None.

claim: In-context graph structure appears in activations abruptly as context grows (square grid, ring, hex grid); Dirichlet energy over the graph tracks accuracy.
agent_test: Check whether more worked traversals of the task graph improve the agent's map.

claim: LLMs may store relations as pairwise links composed on demand, not a global coordinate map (Qin 2026); a hybrid model switches between heuristic and map inference by context length; a shortest-path model scored 0 percent at other context lengths.
agent_test: Test queries needing global layout vs pairwise composition; the map format may need to be a relation list, not coordinates.

claim: Transformers trained on aliased-room navigation: LSTM 99.00 percent accuracy but beat a fallback path only 29.53 percent; bottleneck variants 96.59-99.55 percent improvement.
agent_test: Training-based; low relevance.

claim: A checked transition model outside the model (code verifier over a graph of actions, preconditions, effects) lifts success even for frontier models: Claude Sonnet 5 38.6 to 99.4, GPT-5.6 Sol 24.6 to 99.2 on a 100-instruction BEHAVIOR-1K subset; Qwen3-4B 2.4 to 75.2.
agent_test: Add a code or rule-based legality check of each planned move against the written map; measure invalid-move rate and success. The gain is from verification, not from the map text itself.

claim: An agent's own imagined state transitions are often wrong: hallucinated-state rate 17.1 to 31.8 percent across four backbones, and 19.3 to 25.2 percent for direct, CoT, replan and verifier agents; grounding cut it to 1.4-10.9 percent. A model-based self-verifier cut invalid actions (6.2 percent) but barely cut hallucinated states.
agent_test: Measure edge/state hallucination of the agent's own written map against ground truth; compare self-check with an external check. Weak backbones only; frontier unmeasured.

claim: Benefit of an explicit grounded map shrinks with model strength in prompt-level comparisons but does not reach zero: Hybrid-WM gain +26 (Llama-3-8B) to +4 (GPT-4o-mini); MAP and Yan gains vanish on strong models (K18). Break-even model size not located.
agent_test: Run the map vs no-map test at three model strengths on the same task; fit the gain against strength.

claim: Few-shot map prompting does not transfer the trained-map benefit: 0-4 demonstrations gave 0-10 percent for o1, GPT-4o and Llama-3 on gridworld path planning, while o1 with no map prompt gave 38 percent at 4-shot. Many-shot untested.
agent_test: Do not add a mandatory map-writing step for a strong reasoner without an equal-token control; allow map as optional.

claim: Frontier multimodal models build poor maps from perception: landmark IoU below 5 percent, F1 under 35 percent, planning success 5.54 percent (target) and 3.76 percent (path); a trained hierarchical map beat a flat grid map.
agent_test: When the agent builds its map from raw task text or images, check each edge before planning.

claim: Humans use both a vector (direction) and a transition (adjacency) map and switch between them; deep RL agents show a similar mix (N=401, 73.8 percent vector choice in open grids, 63.6 in cluttered). The only format guidance is by analogy: offer both views. No LLM prompt-format comparison exists.
agent_test: Test relation-list only vs adjacency plus coordinates vs both on the same graph tasks at equal tokens.

claim: Abstract structure transfer is behaviourally strong but the neural map forms slowly: N=28 transfer t(27)=9.54; abstract graph code in mPFC appears only at the second scan, 1 to 7 days later (N=22, p=0.003), with no entorhinal effect.
agent_test: Not agent-testable; do not read as support for in-prompt maps.
